description: Silent-pass defects in code this project did not write, each anchored to a real fix commit in the upstream repository. Ground truth is the upstream maintainers' own decision that the pre-fix behaviour was wrong, not our judgment.
status: Q1-intersection: 17/17 adjudicated. Q2 sample: 40/40 adjudicated of a 140-candidate pool (seed 20260821); 100 remain UNADJUDICATED. 3 cases accepted across both runs. Recall of the harvest is unknown; SP-EXT is a lower bound and is never quoted as a rate.
inclusion_rule: R1 a reachable path existed where the measurement did not happen
R2 on that path the value was INDISTINGUISHABLE from a real healthy measurement
R3 the fix made the absence visible
adjudication: three independent reviewers per candidate, each assigned a distinct lens and each prompted to REJECT; accepted only when rejecters fail to reach a majority; uncertainty resolves to REJECT
recall: UNKNOWN. Candidates come from a frozen commit-message regex intersected with a frozen diff shape. Fixes described some other way are invisible to it. SP-EXT is a LOWER BOUND on incidence and must never be quoted as a rate.

cases.fix_subject: fix(checks)!: return None from SuiteResult.pass_rate when nothing evaluated (#2753)
cases.what_failed: the suite evaluated nothing — an empty suite, or every scenario skipped, or the producing probe crashed
cases.why_it_reads_healthy: the pre-fix DOCSTRING documented the flattering default as intended behaviour — '1.0 when all scenarios are skipped' — so a consumer reading 1.0 was reading the documented contract, and a suite that evaluated nothing was indistinguishable from one in which everything passed
cases.consumer: the Rich console summary line 'Summary: … | Pass Rate: 100.0%'; the Giskard Hub upload payload via to_hub_format/model_dump, which shipped 1.0 as a genuine success_rate; the project's own README example print(f'Aggregated pass rate: {results.pass_rate * 100}%'); and user CI gates thresholding the field
cases.fix: the zero-denominator branch returns None, the signature becomes float | None, the console renders '—' when None, and the Hub payload serialises the absence
cases.prefix_docstring: pass_rate : float — Fraction of non-skipped scenarios that passed (1.0 when all scenarios are skipped).
cases.consumer_evidence: confirmed by the fix's own diff: the README example was changed to handle None, tests/export/test_hub.py was extended (the Hub payload carried the value), and the garak scan adapter was updated — three distinct consumers touched by the one fix
cases.verification: read directly from git at dd75e974ee by the author of this entry, not taken from the adjudicating agents. An earlier draft of this record named the module as giskard/core/suite.py, which does not exist; corrected before publication.
cases.defect_line_verified: git show dd75e974ee~1:libs/giskard-checks/src/giskard/checks/core/result.py line 636 is `return 1.0`, inside `if denominator == 0:` at 635

cases.fix_subject: fix(web_browser): warn once when AppKit is missing on the macOS scale-factor probe
cases.what_failed: the optional dependency pyobjc-framework-AppKit was not installed, so `from AppKit import NSScreen` raised ModuleNotFoundError inside a bare `except Exception`
cases.why_it_reads_healthy: 1.0 is a LEGITIMATE scale factor — every non-HiDPI display measures exactly 1.0 — so a consumer cannot distinguish 'measured, and this screen is not HiDPI' from 'AppKit is missing and we guessed'
cases.consumer: the web_browser tool's screenshot and coordinate scaling on headful macOS; a HiDPI screen silently treated as 1x produces mis-scaled coordinates with no error anywhere
cases.fix: ModuleNotFoundError is caught separately and emits a functools.cache'd logger.warning naming the missing package
cases.fix_strength_note: PARTIAL by the standards of this corpus: the fix still RETURNS 1.0. The absence became visible to a human reading logs, not to a program reading the value. R3 is satisfied because the frozen rule lists 'a warning', but a consumer that thresholds the number still cannot distinguish the two cases.
cases.verification: path and line read directly from `git show --name-only` and the pre-fix source. An earlier draft of this entry invented the path 'src/inspect_ai/tool/_tools/_web_browser/_resources/scale.py', which does not exist — the SECOND fabricated path in this corpus today, both caught by checking rather than by re-reading my own text.
cases.defect_line_verified: git show acd139cc75~1:<module> line 30 is `return 1.0`, inside `except Exception:` at 29, guarding the AppKit import at 26
cases.sibling_note: the same file has a second `except Exception: return 1.0` at line 42 for the Windows DPI probe, which this fix did NOT touch — an unfixed instance of the same shape, recorded rather than claimed

cases.defect_line_verified: git show a8d473e40450~1:<module> line 308 is `return True` in __instancecheck__ (307); line 311 is the same in __subclasscheck__ (310)
cases.subtype_note: the adjudicators labelled it SP-1 HEALTHY_ON_CRASH 2/3 with one abstention; recorded as SP-4 because the value is consumed as a GATE, and the disagreement is disclosed rather than resolved by fiat
cases.what_failed: an optional dependency failed to import, so the symbol was replaced by a `Dummy` placeholder
cases.what_was_returned: isinstance(anything, MissingOptionalClass) -> True, for any object
cases.why_it_reads_healthy: True is exactly what a genuine type match returns. Code guarded by `if isinstance(x, SomeOptionalClass):` takes the branch as though the object really were that type, so a missing dependency reads as a satisfied type check rather than as an absence
cases.consumer: every isinstance/issubclass guard in the codebase that names an optionally-imported class; the pre-fix tree contains 291 isinstance call sites, and any of them naming a Dummy-substituted symbol matched unconditionally
cases.fix: both return False, plus a docstring warning: 'While dummies can be used as types, they return false to all isinstance' — failing closed instead of open
cases.verification: diff, pre-fix source and line numbers read directly from git by the corpus author

overturned.candidate: inspect_ai 34beafda81 — Prevent math scorer from executing model output (#4361)
overturned.adjudication: 2 of 3 reviewers failed to reject it, so the protocol ACCEPTED it
overturned.overturned_by: direct reading of the pre-fix source by the corpus author
overturned.reason: The claim was that `parse_answer` returns None when every parse route fails and `check_answers` short-circuits. It does: `if ans1 is None or ans2 is None: return False`, and `score()` then emits Score(value=INCORRECT). So an unparseable TARGET marks the model WRONG. That fails CLOSED — the alarming direction. R2 requires a value indistinguishable from a HEALTHY measurement, and INCORRECT is not one. The single reviewer who rejected it was right and the majority was wrong.
overturned.note: Recorded because 'every verdict is published so a reader can overturn a label rather than trust it' is only worth writing if the first reader actually does it. A 2-of-3 majority is not evidence; the source is.
